sections.introduction: Pannalapatiryadi Ghrita is a classical Ayurvedic medicated ghee formulation indicated in Visha Roga (toxic conditions and poisoning). This formulation is a complex polyherbal preparation composed of Kwatha (decoction), Svarasa (fresh juices), and Kalka (herbal paste) processed in Murchita Goghrita (purified cow’s ghee). It is designed to neutralize toxins, support vital organs, and restore systemic balance. The formulation includes multiple Vishaghna (anti-toxic), Rasayana (rejuvenative), and Deepana-Pachana (digestive) herbs, making it highly effective in managing both acute and chronic toxic conditions.

पाठा जया गारुडी च पंचांगं च शिरीषजम् ।। 
बिल्वं मधूकं वसुकं सर्पगन्धा फलत्रयम्। 
नील्युशीरे च एतैस्तु कषायं कारयेद्भिषक् ।। 
अपामार्गो व्याघ्रपादी नेयबल्ली विम्बिपत्रकम् ।। 
दशपुष्पाणि ब्रह्मी च एतेषां स्वरसस्तथा।। 
स्वरसग्रहणार्थ तु नीरं योज्यं कषायकम्। 
पूर्वोक्तस्येति तु मतं ज्ञेयं च विषहारिणाम् ।। 
हिंगुर्वचा च लशुनः यष्टीमधुकमेव च। 
अश्वगन्धा जीरके द्वे मृद्धीका चन्दनं तथा।। 
वरा कुष्ठं च तक्कोलं पद्मवीजं कटुत्रयम्। 
कल्कार्थ चापि दत्वाऽथ साधयेद्धृतमुत्तमम् ।। 
सारमेयविषं हन्ति गोपनीयं प्रयत्नतः ।।

 Bimbi Patra (Coccinia grandis — Ivy gourd leaves) — 80 gm

 III. Ghrita Dravya

 IV. Kalka Dravyas (Herbal Paste Ingredients)

 Method Of Preparation 
 First, the Kwatha (decoction) is prepared by boiling Kwatha Dravyas (decoction ingredients) in water and reducing it to one-fourth. Separately, Kalka Dravyas (paste ingredients) are made into a fine paste and mixed thoroughly with Murchita Goghrita (processed cow’s ghee). Then the prepared decoction is added to this mixture. Next, Svarasa Dravyas (juice ingredients) are processed to extract their juices (or reduced decoction where necessary) and added to the mixture. The entire preparation is then subjected to mild heating following classical Sneha Paka Vidhi (medicated ghee preparation process) until only medicated ghrita remains. After achieving proper Sneha Siddhi Lakshanas (signs of completion), the formulation is filtered and stored in clean, wide-mouthed glass containers.

Visha Roga (poisoning and toxic conditions) 
 Chronic toxin accumulation

 Therapeutic Properties 
 This formulation is a comprehensive anti-toxic preparation. Sirisha (Albizia lebbeck) and Apamarga (Achyranthes aspera) are well-known Vishaghna herbs that help neutralize toxins. Triphala—Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Vibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis)—supports detoxification and digestion. Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina) provides calming and systemic regulatory effects. Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) enhances nervous system stability, while Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) improves strength and resilience. The inclusion of multiple floral juices enhances subtle detoxification and systemic cleansing. Goghrita (cow’s ghee) acts as a Yogavahi (carrier), ensuring deep tissue penetration and nourishment.
sections.precautions:
Should be used strictly under medical supervision 
 Use cautiously in pregnancy and lactation 
 Monitor for digestive tolerance 
 Not advised in individuals with weak digestion without prior Deepana therapy 

 Conclusion 
 Pannalapatiryadi Ghrita is a highly potent and complex Ayurvedic formulation designed for managing Visha Roga (toxic conditions). Its multi-layered preparation involving decoction, fresh juices, and herbal paste enhances its therapeutic efficacy. When administered properly, it helps neutralize toxins, restore physiological balance, and strengthen overall health, making it a valuable formulation in Ayurvedic toxicology and systemic detoxification.
